titleEn: When the Train's in Sight, It's All Right!

pages.text: The train stopped at the kindergarten station. "I won't get off!" Bami gripped the sleeping-car quilt in their beak. It was their first day at kindergarten.

Mom lifted the quilt gently. "Dad and I will go to the next station, then stop here at lunch and again in the evening." Bami's eyes filled. "I want to stay with the train..." Kindergarten stood on a yellow-flower hill outside.
A goat carrying a roll book entered. "Is Bami here? Attendance!" She was the teacher. Her unfamiliar voice sent Bami deeper under the quilt. "New teacher, new friends... Scary."
The teacher sat gently by the bed. "Everyone feels a little nervous at first. Look outside with me?" Bami peeked out. She pointed. "You can see this same train from our classroom window."
She whispered, "Dad's train stops here at lunch. When the train's in sight, it's all right!" Bami came out and stood close to her. "When the train's in sight... it's all right?"
The kindergarten room on the flowered hill bustled with new friends. Bami went straight to the window. Dad's train stood at the platform, and Mom waved from the dining car.

Toot! The train slowly left, and Bami's heart thumped again. The teacher came beside them. "When the train's in sight, it's all right! It comes back at lunch. Until then, build blocks with your friends?" Bami turned and took a step toward them.
Building blocks and playing tag soon brought lunchtime. Toot! Bami ran to the window. Dad's train stood below the flowered hill! Wings wide, Bami called, "When the train's in sight, it's all right!"
Mom came that evening. Bami, who had cried that morning, now ran smiling. "I made friends! I want to come tomorrow! One, look outside! Two, play with friends! Three, wave when the train comes!"

On the train, Mom wrapped Bami in her wings like a piggyback hug. "You did so well, even when nervous!" A little courage had filled a new place with friends. When the train's in sight, it's all right!
